text.p: Courtaulds Plc chief executive Gordon Campbell said on Wednesday that the international chemicals group was "in pretty good shape", despite concerns over viscose and sterling's strength.

"We have a problem with viscose, which is 10 percent of sales, we have some worries about the value of sterling, but apart from that I think most of our businesses are in very good shape," Campbell told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Campbell, who took charge of the group last July, said viscose would continue to account for a dwindling proportion of sales as the group's efforts were focused on coatings, polymer products and the successful new fibre, Tencel.
Courtaulds is Europe's biggest producer of viscose, which he said had had "a pretty dreadful year."

Campbell said in February that the market for the product, which has been hit by overcapacity and changes in fashion, showed "a few signs of recovery, and that is still where I am." Courtaulds had no plans to add to the cuts in production announced earlier this year, he added.

The group's newest fibre Tencel, a fabric derived from woodpulp, moved "clearly into profit" in the year to March despite costs associated with developing new production capacity in Grimsby, England, and Alabama.

A decision on a new production facility in the Far East would be made sooner rather than later, with an announcement expected in the second half of the year. Campbell told Reuters that the competition for the plant was between Korea, Indonesia and Singapore.
